cases.use: a lab procedure step, from a handout

issues: Sheets 05-13: the 'pink' is never pink. The flash where the drop lands is a mustard-yellow ellipse and the endpoint fill is olive/khaki; the one visual fact the clip exists to teach (faint pink that lasts) is shown in the wrong color, actively mis-teaching what to look for

Sheets 01-13: the apparatus is a small thin-line burette and flask pinned mid-frame occupying maybe a quarter of the 9:16 canvas; the bottom third is empty chalkboard and the flask (where all the action happens) is tiny, so drops and the color change are hard to see on a phone

Sheets 06-10: the flash/fade/linger cycle reads as the same blob appearing and dimming; there is no visible difference between 'flashes then fades' and 'starts to linger', no swirl motion, and no visible slowing of drop rate for 'drop by drop', so motion does not carry the narration's meaning

tickets: demo_unsettled: Phase 1 of e2's demo (fast, 6.5 to 13.4 s) should end on the finished state, but "additions into the flask" is still changing at 13.3 s, 0.00 s before it ends; it never rests on the result.

demo_unsettled: Phase 1 of e3's demo (slow, 13.4 to 18.1 s) should end on the finished state, but "additions into the flask" is still changing at 18.0 s, 0.00 s before it ends; it never rests on the result.

cases.use: a horror beat whose subject stays hidden

issues: Sheets 01-12: the look fights the brief. A bright cream paper background with a flat brown box for the lake reads as daytime infographic, not a campfire story; there is no darkness, no night, no depth below the surface, so nothing feels like it could be hiding under the dock

Sheets 06-11: the rope 'going tight' is a single snap from a slack curve to a straight line, then nothing. No strain, no tremor, no tug, no pull on the post, no ripple at the entry point; once taut the frame is effectively a still for 12 seconds, so the 'something is holding it' feeling is never built

Sheets 08-09: the slow push-in during the silence is the one good instinct, but it reverses at about 16.9 s (sheet 09) and snaps back out to the wide shot, releasing the tension exactly when 'She didn't move' should tighten it

cases.use: a 16:9 lesson on a TV across a room

issues: Sheets 01-14: the water is painted khaki/sand while the ground under it is pale blue; the color code is inverted, so a 9-year-old reads the blue as water and the tan as land, and 'water fills the chamber' looks like the chamber filling with sand

Sheets 12-13: the upper gate opening, the final step the clip promises, is a thin dark line that simply vanishes; no swing, no gap opening, no emphasis, and 'levels match' is only a faint dashed line, so the payoff step is nearly invisible across a living room

Sheets 01-14: the bottom caption is printed directly on the diagram's base, overlapping the tiny 'LOWER CANAL / CHAMBER' labels, and is set in small tracked caps; it collides on every frame and is hard to read at 3 m

tickets: flat_rhythm: The picture changes at nearly the same rate all through (e1 0.47, e2 0.85, e3 0.65, e4 0.82 steps a second; spread 0.22). The plan mixes long and short events, but the scene does not.

demo_unsettled: Phase 1 of e3's demo (slow, 14.3 to 20.3 s) should end on the finished state, but "the chamber filling and the boat rising" is still changing at 20.3 s, 0.00 s before it ends; it never rests on the result.

issues: Sheets 05, 08, 09, 10: cards never move. Every 'slide' is an in-place swap of the digits inside fixed boxes, done in about a quarter second, so 'the one slides in front' and 'it passes the four' are never seen as a card travelling past others; the user's 'show the first insert slowly' is not delivered (the first insert at 8.3-8.5 s is the fastest-looking event in the clip)

Sheets 05-10: the arrow stays parked on a slot instead of riding with the card being inserted; after the first swap it points at the 4 (sheet 05, 9.0 s onward) and after the 3's insert it points at the 4 again, so the eye follows the wrong card
Sheets 05 and 08: the comparison is never shown; there is no '4 > 1' or 'stops at 1 < 3' mark, just both cards turning orange, so the viewer cannot describe one insertion's logic
